## Description

Both single-leg movements on Hips day ran off an ankle cuff on a low pulley — the attachment that gets avoided in practice. This moves hip extension to the standing glute kickback machine and hip flexion to a captain's chair knee raise. The day keeps all four of its hip actions (adduction, abduction, extension, flexion); only the equipment changes.

Each replacement carries the cue that separates it from its failure mode, found on the floor rather than inferred:

- **Glute Kickback (Machine)** — driving through the heel with a free knee turns the movement into a backwards single-leg press. It registers as quad instead of glute, so the note pins the knee angle and tells the pelvis to stay quiet rather than letting the low back supply the range.
- **Knee Raise** — keeps the psoas-above-90 cue from the cable entry it replaces, and adds the pelvis tell: a neutral pelvis keeps the work in hip flexion, curling it toward the ribs hands the work to the abs.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Infrastructure change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor

## Changes Made

Adds `backend/migrations/005-hips-machine-swaps.js`. No other files touched.

| Removed | Added |
| --- | --- |
| Cable Glute Kickback (ankle cuff, low pulley) | Glute Kickback (Machine) — extension |
| Cable Standing Leg Raise (same cuff) | Knee Raise, captain's chair — flexion |

No model version bump. The cycle's days are unchanged and only the exercise library moves, so this follows the pattern in `003-dumbbell-cable-press.js` rather than `004-synergy-17-shoulder-press.js`. The hips day number is read from the active model rather than hardcoded.

Existing logged workouts are unaffected. A `logged-workout` stores its exercises inline by name, so removing a library entry cannot reach back and rewrite history.

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [ ] Workflow passes
- [ ] Deployment verified

Ran the migration twice against the repo's in-memory container (`backend/migrations/memory-container.js`): the first pass reports `{ dayNumber: 17, created: 2, removed: 2 }` and the second `{ created: 0, removed: 0 }` — a clean no-op rather than a 404, which is the re-runnability requirement.

`node --test` in `backend/` passes (7 tests), as does `scripts/next-app-version.test.mjs`.

One issue caught during that run and fixed before commit: the first draft filtered with `c.daySlug = @daySlug`, which the in-memory container has no clause for. That would have made `npm run migrate:dry-run` silently return the entire exercise library instead of the hips subset. It now queries by type and filters in code, matching `004`.

Container build is left to CI per the repo's guidance on agent pods.

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed the code
- [x] Updated documentation if needed
- [x] No breaking changes (or documented if necessary)

`CLAUDE.md` names no individual Hips day exercises, so it needs no edit for this change.

## Related Issues

None.

## Screenshots

N/A — no layout change. The Exercises and Today views render the new entries through the existing components.

## Deployment Notes

This migration runs at pod startup with `RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_BOOT=true` and writes to the live Cosmos container. It deletes two `exercise` documents and creates two others. A failure exits the process and fails the rollout by design.

One follow-up deliberately left out of scope: `frontend/src/utils/sorenessLink.js:42` maps hips day to `['Hip & Adductors', 'Glutes']`. The knee raise adds real ab/core involvement, so `Abs & Core` is arguably missing from that suggestion list now.
